title: Crown HVAC Footage Reorg Report
summary: Footage reorganization report for Crown HVAC shoot split into two locations.
content:
Editor's Guide: Ambition Mechanical - Crown HVAC Service (Two Locations)

Date of Shoot: March 5, 2026 Reorganized: March 11, 2026 (v2: split into two locations, v3: renamed with real location context) Source: /Volumes/SS8TB/Ambition Mechanical Services/20260305 Crown/

Overview

This shoot covers two distinct locations, separated by a ~24-minute gap (likely travel/setup time).

Metric Crown Room (Rooftop) Memorial Tower (Mechanical Room) Total
Video clips 35 Ronin4D + 7 Drone 31 Ronin4D 73
Audio files 3 lav recordings 0 3
Photos 5 drone aerials 0 5
Time window 8:50 - 9:24 AM (+ drone 9:24-9:52) 9:48 - 10:10 AM --
Total files 47 34 81

Location Context

Crown Room - Likely the Crown at Hotel San Carlos, a historic downtown Phoenix hotel built in 1928. Seven stories, Italian Renaissance Revival architecture, listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The "Crown Room" refers to a restaurant/event space within the hotel. The kitchen fire would have required HVAC restoration work including: commercial kitchen exhaust hood replacement, rooftop exhaust fan units (visible in footage), smoke/soot remediation of ductwork, and potentially makeup air systems for the kitchen. Historic buildings like this add complexity: older duct runs, tight mechanical spaces, code compliance upgrades during restoration. The rooftop footage showing exhaust fan disassembly is consistent with replacing fire-damaged kitchen ventilation equipment.

Memorial Tower - A senior living high-rise in Phoenix. Senior housing facilities typically run centralized chiller/boiler plants with Trane or similar commercial controls (consistent with the Trane control panels visible in C0042-C0043). The mechanical room footage shows extensive piping, pumps, valves, and chiller units, which is characteristic of a central plant serving a multi-story residential building. HVAC systems in senior facilities must maintain strict temperature and air quality standards for vulnerable residents. A long-term project at a facility like this could involve chiller replacement, building automation upgrades, or full mechanical system modernization. The scale of piping and equipment visible in the footage suggests this is the main mechanical plant for the entire building.

Total duration (video): ~28 min Total audio duration: ~61 min (3 lav recordings) Total size: ~105 GB

Crown Room (C0004-C0035, 8:50 - 9:24 AM)

Location: Crown Room, likely at Hotel San Carlos, downtown Phoenix. Historic 1928 building. Kitchen fire restoration project.

Exterior rooftop exhaust fan replacement responding to kitchen fire damage. Gravel roof with HVAC units, parking garage arrival/departure, and interior kitchen walkthrough. Workers in safety vests disassembling old exhaust fans. The commercial kitchen exhaust system needed full replacement after fire damage. Also includes all drone aerials (shot 9:24-9:52 AM while crew moved locations) and all lav audio (recorded 7:48-8:55 AM during early rooftop work).

Story angle: Ambition restoring a piece of Phoenix history. A kitchen fire in a nearly 100-year-old building is high-stakes work: the HVAC crew has to bring modern code compliance to a historic structure. The rooftop exhaust fans are the visible part of the kitchen ventilation system that keeps a commercial kitchen safe and operational.

Lav Sync Analysis (March 11):

  • Lav audio was recorded 7:48-8:55 AM AZ time (pre-camera work)
  • Crown Room video starts at 8:50 AM. Only B006C0004 (5.7s establishing shot) overlaps with Lav 3 at offset 2:07
  • Memorial Tower video starts at 9:48 AM, well after all lav recordings ended
  • The lav audio captured the crew's early morning work sounds before the cinema camera rolled
  • For editing: these lavs are best used as ambient work audio / SFX, not interview sync
  • All talking shots (Crown Room + Memorial Tower) rely on camera mic audio only

Memorial Tower (C0036-C0069, 9:48 - 10:10 AM)

Location: Memorial Tower, Phoenix. Senior living facility. Long-term HVAC project nearing completion.

Indoor mechanical/equipment room serving a senior residential high-rise. Extensive piping, valves, pumps, Trane control panels, chiller units. This is the central plant that keeps residents comfortable year-round. This is where the HERO talking walkthrough was shot (C0037). The crew member walks through explaining HVAC systems while pointing at equipment. All the pipe/valve detail shots form a cohesive rapid-fire sequence.

Story angle: Ambition keeping seniors safe and comfortable. The scale of the mechanical room (chillers, pumps, building automation) shows this isn't a quick service call. It's a long-term relationship maintaining critical infrastructure for vulnerable residents. The Trane control panels and chiller systems are the kind of commercial-grade equipment that requires specialized HVAC expertise.

Gap Analysis: What's Missing

  1. No before/after shots. No "before" state of the old equipment to contrast with the new install.
  2. Only one camera angle on talking shots. C0037 is all one angle/take. A B-camera or alternate framing would help.
  3. No client/building manager testimonial. Having the Crown facility manager on camera would be gold for case studies.
  4. No finished product shots. We see work in progress but not the completed install.
  5. No Ambition logo/branding hero shot on-site. The truck shots show the truck but a deliberate hero shot would be stronger.
  6. No team portrait/group shot. Social media loves showing the crew together.
  7. Indoor kitchen footage is limited. C0033 and C0034 are mostly walkthrough.
  8. No lav audio for Memorial Tower. The mechanical room talking shots (including HERO C0037) may only have camera mic audio. This is the biggest audio gap.

Edit Recommendations

60s Project Showcase (Instagram Reel / LinkedIn)

  • Open: C0035 (crew walking to truck in parking garage) OR drone 0007 (building orbit) [Crown Room]
  • :05-:15: C0017 (hero rooftop shot), C0005 (wide rooftop work) [Crown Room]
  • :15-:35: Process montage: C0006 (disassembly), C0025 (teamwork), C0027 (reaching into duct) [Crown Room]
  • :35-:45: Detail rapid-fire: Cut through C0045-C0055 (pipe/valve sequence) [Memorial Tower]
  • :45-:55: C0037 talking head pull quote (check lav sync) [Memorial Tower]
  • :55-:60: Drone 0013 (4K wide pull) as closer [Crown Room]

30s IG Reel (High Energy)

  • Quick cuts between C0006 process, C0056 pump detail, C0027 hands-in-duct
  • Speed ramp the process footage (24fps ProRes holds up to speed ramps)
  • C0037 one-liner as voiceover (2-3 seconds max)
  • End on drone establishing

Long-form Case Study (2-3 min)

  • C0037 is the spine. Cut between the walking tour and b-roll that matches what he's pointing at.
  • Use Crown Room footage for rooftop action, Memorial Tower for equipment room depth.
  • Drone aerials as chapter breaks between the two locations.
  • Detail sequence as interstitial.

Technical Reference

All Ronin4D footage: ProRes 4K (3840x2160) at 24fps, PCM 24-bit 48kHz stereo All Drone footage: HEVC 2.7K (2688x1512) or 4K (3840x2160) at 59.94fps All Lav audio: PCM 32-bit float 48kHz mono

Color: Footage appears to be shot in a flat/log profile. Needs color grade.
